title: Balanced Brackets
statement:
The string s contains only the six characters ( ) [ ] { }. Return true if every bracket is closed properly, and false otherwise.

Closed properly means three things: every opening bracket has a closing bracket of the same kind, brackets close in the reverse order they were opened, and no closing bracket appears without an open one waiting for it.

examples.why: The braces and the parentheses both open and close inside the square brackets.
Each kind appears once open and once closed, so counting per kind says yes. But ) arrives while [ is the most recent open bracket, so the nesting is broken.
Nothing closes wrongly, but one ( is still open when the string ends.

hints: When you meet a closing bracket, which opening bracket does it have to match?
It must match the most recent opening bracket that is still unmatched. Which structure gives you "the most recent unmatched thing" in O(1)?
Push every opening bracket on a stack. On a closing bracket, the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the same kind; pop it. At the end the stack must be empty.

explain.intuition:
Brackets nest like HTML tags: <div><span></div> is broken because the inner tag must close first. The bracket that a closer has to match is always the latest one still open. "Latest still open" is exactly what the top of a stack holds.

So push openers, and let each closer pop the top and check that the kinds agree. Counting brackets per kind is not enough, because counts ignore order: ([)] has perfect counts and is still wrong.
steps: Map each closer to its opener: ) → (, ] → [, } → {.
Walk the string. For an opener, push it on the stack.
For a closer, if the stack is empty or its top is not the matching opener, return false. Otherwise pop.
After the walk, return whether the stack is empty: leftover openers were never closed.
pitfalls: Popping from an empty stack on input like )(. In JavaScript pop() returns undefined quietly; in Python it throws.
Returning true at the end without checking that the stack is empty, which accepts (().
Using one counter per bracket kind. It cannot see crossings like ([)].

solutions.title: Erase matched pairs until nothing changes
solutions.idea: A balanced string always has an adjacent pair like () somewhere. Keep deleting adjacent pairs; the string is balanced exactly when it ends up empty.

solutions.title: Stack of open brackets
solutions.idea: Push openers. A closer must match the opener on top of the stack, which is the most recent one still open.

followups: The string also contains letters and other characters that should be ignored. What changes?
Only one kind of bracket, ( and ). Can you do it in O(1) extra space?
